newsitem.title: SPAIN: Chirac urges Ukraine to pursue reform for IMF aid.
newsitem.headline: Chirac urges Ukraine to pursue reform for IMF aid.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told Ukraine on Wednesday to pursue economic reform, speed up privatisation and make its economy more transparent if it wanted more international financial aid, a French official said.
President Leonid Kuchma, meeting Chirac on the margins of a NATO summit in Madrid, appealed to the French leader for support for Ukraine's drive for International Monetary Fund (IMF) loans.
The IMF said recently it might delay a three-year $2.5-$3 billion loan meant for countries undertaking structural reforms and issue a limited stand-by loan in the meantime.

The French official said Chirac praised Kiev's recent signature of an agreement with Russia settling outstanding disputes but listed a series of steps Ukraine needed to take to win further Western financial backing.
He cited a need to accelerate privatisation of state enterprises, which has proceeded at a snail's pace, pursue structural reforms and establish laws on transparency and stability.
The French leader also recalled a pledge by Ukraine -- site of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in 1986 -- to bring its former Soviet nuclear power plants up to Western safety standards.
He deplored the fact that some Western countries had not yet met their commitments under a Group of Seven agreement to finance the programme.
Chirac told reporters he had pressed the issue in a private meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday.
